scope: SCOPE IS PARTIAL AND DELIBERATELY SO. This record audits the prior review FB2-REV-000001. The review schema does not permit FB2-REV-000001 itself to appear in reviewed_ids or in a findings[].artifact_id: review.schema.json constrains both to '^FB2-[A-Z]{2,3}-[A-Z]{2,3}-[0-9]{6}$', which requires three dash-separated segments, while a review artifact id has only two. A review of a review record is structurally unrepresentable and is recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000184 rather than worked around. To audit a review record at all, this meta review necessarily re-covers the artifacts that review declared; that re-coverage is enumerated below and is a schema limitation, not additional coverage. FB2-VER-EXE-000001 is excluded because it was revised to revision 2 by a concurrent session during this pass and its content has moved; it is the subject of FB2-REV-FND-000174 in FB2-REV-000010. This record does not review itself.

findings.description: Reviewed_ids cannot express which profile was reviewed, and in this corpus that is a live ambiguity rather than a theoretical one. review.schema.json allows exactly artifact_id, revision and digest in each reviewed_ids item, with additionalProperties false, so there is no profile field. Every artifact FB2-REV-000001 claims to have reviewed exists in BOTH the as_is and the synthetic_reference profile with different content. Only the digest disambiguates them, and only because the digest is a real content hash. Of the 16 recorded digests that could be re-checked against current content, all 16 match the as_is file byte for byte and none matches the corresponding synthetic_reference file, so the prior record is correct on those. It is structurally fragile: a reader applying an artifact_id to the wrong profile would review different content while believing they had reviewed the reviewed one. The review records authored by this pass state the profile span explicitly in their scope field to compensate; the prior record does not.
findings.evidence: review.schema.json reviewed_ids.items properties are artifact_id, revision, digest with additionalProperties false. 16 of the prior record's 17 digests equal the sha256 of the as_is file and differ from the synthetic_reference file. The 17th, for FB2-VER-EXE-000001, is now stale - see FB2-REV-FND-000174.

findings.description: The prior review's dispositions use resolved_artifact_id to point at the artifact each finding is raised against rather than at an artifact created to resolve it. The schema documents the field as 'Optional ID of artifact created to resolve this finding'. Example: finding FB2-FND-000001 is raised against FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 and dispositioned 'accepted' with resolved_artifact_id 'FB2-SAF-FSR-000001'. The same self-referential pattern appears in all five dispositions. No artifact was created to resolve any of the five findings, so a reader could conclude that resolving artifacts exist when none do. Recorded, not corrected: FB2-REV-000001 was not modified.
findings.evidence: FB2-REV-000001 dispositions: FB2-FND-000002 -> 'FB2-SW-SWR-000001' (finding on FB2-SW-SWR-000001); FB2-FND-000003 -> 'FB2-HW-TSR-000001' (finding on FB2-HW-TSR-000001); FB2-FND-000004 -> 'FB2-SW-DSN-000002' (finding on FB2-SW-DSN-000002); FB2-FND-000005 -> 'FB2-VER-TMS-000001' (finding on FB2-VER-TMS-000001). Each action text says the work is still to be done.

findings.description: Re-verification of the prior review's five findings: four hold and one holds with corrected arithmetic. FB2-FND-000002 (host-run publish latency not verified on target), FB2-FND-000003 (AFE accuracy from datasheet, not measured), FB2-FND-000004 (debounce count unjustified) and FB2-FND-000005 (unit test does not cover end-to-end timing) were each confirmed against the artifact content and none is affected by the concurrent rewrite, because all five name artifacts outside the rewritten execution population. FB2-FND-000001 (timing budget) is upheld but its arithmetic was incomplete; the corrected derivation is FB2-REV-FND-000171. Recorded as a performed check so the prior review's quality is attributable to verification rather than silence.
findings.evidence: FB2-REV-000001 findings FB2-FND-000002..FB2-FND-000005 confirmed against FB2-SW-SWR-000001, FB2-HW-TSR-000001, FB2-SW-DSN-000002 and FB2-VER-TMS-000001; all four artifacts re-hashed and unchanged. FB2-FND-000001 upheld with corrected arithmetic, see FB2-REV-FND-000171.

findings.description: Structural gap in the review framework, discovered while attempting this very meta review: review.schema.json constrains reviewed_ids[].artifact_id and findings[].artifact_id to a three-segment pattern, but review artifact ids have only two segments. The consequence is that no review record can legally list another review record as a reviewed artifact or as the subject of a finding, so review-record quality is structurally outside the review framework meant to cover it. A reader relying on automated_review_coverage would see every review record counted and every review record uncheckable. The workaround used here is to audit the prior review through the artifacts it covered, which is weaker: it cannot bind a finding to the review record itself. No schema was edited and no check was weakened.
findings.evidence: Observed directly: writing a review record with 'FB2-REV-000001' in reviewed_ids produced 7 high-severity schema findings from corpus.py ('schema violation at reviewed_ids/0/artifact_id'). The artifact base schema permits one to three segments via '^FB2(-[A-Z]{2,4}){1,3}-[0-9]{6}$', so review ids are legal as ids but cannot be referenced by review records.

findings.description: The corpus's automated_review_coverage dimension cannot observe review records other than one. corpus.py computes the numerator by loading a single hardcoded file, docs/artifacts/reviews/records/review-vertical-slice.json, and reading only its reviewed_ids. Every other review record in docs/artifacts/reviews/records/ is indexed as an artifact, so it enlarges the DENOMINATOR while contributing nothing to the numerator. This pass demonstrates the effect: adding eleven review records moved the dimension from 17/87 to 17/101 while the numerator stayed at 17. The metric therefore reports review coverage getting worse as review coverage improves, which is the opposite of its intent. The reviewed_by trace links added by this pass carry the information the dimension was meant to express, but the dimension does not read them. No tool change was made: corpus.py is outside this review's write scope and editing a metric to look better would be metric gaming.
findings.evidence: corpus.py line 903: rp = self.artifacts_dir / 'reviews' / 'records' / 'review-vertical-slice.json'; line 905-906: reviewed_ids populated only from that file's reviewed_ids; line 908-909: numerator = len(reviewed_ids & index_ids), denominator = len(index_ids). No other code path aggregates reviewed_ids for this dimension.

dispositions.action: Accepted as a structural limitation of the review schema, not a data error. The prior record is correct as written and was NOT edited. Widening reviewed_ids to carry a profile field would change the schema and invalidate the prior record, both outside this review's write scope. Referred to the schema owner.

Accepted. Recorded as a usage defect in the prior record. FB2-REV-000001 was deliberately not modified: master-prompt section 15 assigns repair to the artifact owner with confirmation by a further pass. Referred to that owner.
No action required. Recorded as a verified result on a performed check.
Accepted. The schema was NOT edited to make this review writable and no validation check was weakened. Referred to the schema owner as a framework gap.

Accepted. corpus.py was NOT modified. The metric defect is recorded so a future tool change can be evaluated on its merits; changing the metric in this pass to report a better number would have been metric gaming and was explicitly avoided.

SCOPE: PARTIAL. This record audits one prior review, FB2-REV-000001, by re-covering the 16 stable artifacts that review declared. It is not a universal review of the as_is profile.

The 16 artifacts listed in reviewed_ids overlap completely with FB2-REV-000010. That overlap is forced by the schema limitation in FB2-REV-FND-000184 and is not additional coverage; the two records use different checklists.

CONCURRENT MODIFICATION, MATERIAL: during this review pass a second session rewrote the as_is execution population. FB2-VER-EXE-000001..000005 moved to revision 2 with different content and eight further as_is execution records (FB2-VER-EXE-000006..000014) were created; the corpus artifact index grew from 87 to 131 entries. This record therefore EXCLUDES all as_is execution artifacts and states that exclusion instead of asserting findings against content that was in motion.

This meta review was performed by the same automated session that authored FB2-REV-000002, FB2-REV-000006, FB2-REV-000008, FB2-REV-000009 and FB2-REV-000010. It is not independent of them, and it relies on the same corpus.py whose behaviour it audits.

Verification performed: (a) all 16 re-checkable reviewed_ids digests in FB2-REV-000001 recomputed from file bytes and cross-checked against both profiles; (b) four of its five findings re-derived against the artifact content they cite; (c) its five dispositions read against the schema's documented meaning of resolved_artifact_id; (d) its reviewer_identity and limitations read for honesty against master-prompt clause 2.9. (a) and (d) clean.

The prior record's reviewer_identity.model is 'nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b' and its session_id is 'review-2026-09-08-001'. This review did not verify that those identifiers are true, because an AI session cannot attest to another session's runtime. They are recorded as asserted by that record.
review_method: Digest recomputation and cross-profile disambiguation for every re-checkable reviewed id in the prior record, independent re-derivation of each re-checkable finding from the cited artifact content, disposition-semantics read against review.schema.json, and a read of corpus.py to determine what the coverage dimension actually measures.
